perspective:
Gloria Bangura’s available information:

- I observed Donald during several company events while he was serving drinks. He seemed distracted and lacked enthusiasm, which made me think he might be unhappy with his job.
- I approached him and asked if he was okay. He told me: “I guess I’m just not as into it as I used to be. It’s kind of repetitive, you know?”
- After that conversation, I reflected on what he said and began to suspect his dissatisfaction at work might be connected to something deeper or more personal.
- I suggested he consider talking to a professional about it. He replied: “I haven’t really considered that, Gloria. I’m not sure if that would help.”
- Afterward, I sensed a shift in Donald’s behavior toward me. I worried he might resent my suggestion and feel I overstepped.
- I apologized and clarified that I only wanted to help because I care. Donald responded: “It’s okay, Gloria. I was a bit taken aback at first, but I know you meant well. It’s just a lot to process.”
- I felt relieved that the tension seemed to ease, and I wanted to strengthen our working relationship.
- I invited Donald to collaborate on an upcoming project, saying it could use his creative input. He said: “Thanks, Gloria. I appreciate it, and yeah, I’d like to be more involved. It sounds like a great opportunity.”
- We collaborated on the project. I observed that Donald contributed significantly and seemed more enthusiastic.
- I believed he was a valuable team member and wanted him to feel appreciated.
- During a team meeting, I publicly acknowledged Donald’s work and said his efforts were crucial to our success.
- Donald thanked me and said: “Thank you, Gloria. That means a lot to me. I’m glad I could contribute and it feels great to be appreciated.”
